meta.title: AI trends to Geneva: metrics for the Orbit Accord simulation
meta.purpose: Measured baselines (through scenario cutoff 2026-11-01) and explicitly labelled extrapolations to the Geneva horizon 2027-06-21, for the educational Orbit Accord / Before Geneva simulation. Research only; no game mechanics are defined here.
meta.retrieval_method: Direct URL fetches of primary sources (no search engine). Epoch pages embed 'Accessed 1 Nov 2026' in their own citation blocks.

evidence_classes.measured: Observed value with a date, published by the named primary source. Quoted, not derived.
evidence_classes.extrapolated: Value computed by extending a published fitted trend past its last observed point; fit, interval and provenance stated.
evidence_classes.judgement: Modelling choice among defensible published alternatives (rate choice, anchor choice, composition).
evidence_classes.fictional: Simulation-only quantity with no data basis: policy-lever effect sizes, drift rates, or any 2026 value for a metric that has no 2026 observation.

honesty_rules: No invented 2026 values: every dated number is quoted from the sources below or derived from quoted numbers and labelled.
Trend-implied levels (e.g. frontier training compute ~3e27 FLOP) are inferences from published statements, not observed model estimates.
Sparse series (chip performance per dollar: ~12 quarters) must not be presented as a smooth exponential; steps are explicit.
Policy-lever effect sizes are fictional and must be labelled as such in any game UI.

sources.title: Trends in AI (dashboard)
sources.carries: Headline rates with 90% CIs: frontier training compute 5x/yr since 2020 (CI 4-6x); training cost 3.5x/yr since 2020 (CI 2.8-4.4x); compute stock 3.4x/yr since 2022 (CI 3.2-3.7x); chip performance per dollar +49%/yr since 2023 (CI 36-66%); ECI frontier +14/yr since reasoning models (CI +12 to +17); context windows 30x/yr since 2023 (CI 10-50x); data-center facts (1.1M H100e Colossus 2; Hyperion 3.7M H100e expected Jan 2028; 71% hyperscaler share; $38B/GW; ~2.1yr GW build time; >$370B raised; 30% of OpenAI 2024 compute spend was inference; OpenAI revenue 3.2x/yr since 2024 CI 3.0-3.4; SOTA on consumer hardware ~8 months).

sources.title: Training compute of frontier AI models grows by 4-5x per year
sources.carries: Log-linear fits with bootstrap CIs on 333 notable-model compute estimates (2010-May 2024): notable 4.1x/yr (90% CI 3.7-4.6); frontier running top-10 5.3x/yr (4.9-5.7); post-2018 frontier 4.2x/yr (3.6-4.9, break 80% CI Oct 2016-Aug 2019, AlphaGo Master/Zero excluded); notable LMs 9.5x/yr (7.4-12.2, Jun 2017-May 2024), ~5.0x/yr (3.1-7.3) after mid-2020; robust to top-N (5.15-5.44 for N=5-20); anchors GPT-3 ~3e23 FLOP (May 2020), GPT-4 ~2e25 (Mar 2023), Gemini Ultra ~5e25 (Dec 2023).

sources.title: Can AI scaling continue through 2030?
sources.carries: 2e29 FLOP training runs likely feasible by 2030; constraints bind in order: power (1-5 GW campuses -> 1e28-3e29 FLOP; distributed 2-45 GW -> 2e28-2e30), chip manufacturing (20M-400M H100e -> 1e29-5e30), data (400T-20Q tokens -> 6e28-2e32), latency wall (3e30-1e32 cap); Llama 3.1 405B = 4e25 FLOP, 16k H100, 27MW, 72 days; 4x/yr exceeds peak mobile adoption (2x/yr 1980-87), solar (1.5x/yr 2001-10), genome sequencing (3.3x/yr 2008-15).

policy_levers.note: Lever EFFECT SIZES are fictional [F] and must be labelled illustrative in any UI. No causal estimate of any real policy on any selected metric exists in the retrieved sources, and none is invented. Starting values and allowed ranges are anchored to measured data [M] where available. Levers are separable by design: exposure, verification, incident response and capability pace change independently.

levers.anchor_measured: Frontier compute 5x/yr (90% CI 4-6x) since 2020; ECI +14/yr (90% CI +12 to +17)
levers.allowed_range: exactly the measured CI: a fictional constraint regime moves the compute rate toward 4x/yr (and ECI slope toward +12); a fictional crash programme toward 6x/yr (+17)
levers.effect_size: fictional: any within-CI shift; suggested display as 'rate moves within the measured band'

levers.changes: deployment exposure (share of measured capability actually exposed in real work)
levers.anchor_measured: July 2026 levels: 20% delegation; 25-57% per-task use; 66% outputs accepted with minor edits; SOTA-on-consumer-hardware within ~8 months
levers.allowed_range: start at measured levels; drift 0-1.5 pp/month is fictional
levers.effect_size: fictional: e.g., liability/procurement/licensing rules shift exposure by a small monthly delta; no causal coefficient exists

levers.changes: verification (probability/latency of detecting a capability milestone or deployment problem in-game)
levers.anchor_measured: Real practice exists and is dated: METR pre-deployment evaluations of GPT-5.6 Sol (2026-06-26) and Claude Opus 5.5 (2026-09-22); Epoch pre-release access to GPT-6 Astra (2026-09-03); ECI hub updates at least monthly (2026-10-01) with daily-weekly data refresh; monitorability evaluations published 2026-01
levers.allowed_range: detection lag of weeks is the realistic anchor; fictional treaty terms (shared evaluations, reporting windows) change it
levers.effect_size: fictional: e.g., joint evaluation regime reduces milestone-detection lag by an illustrative number of weeks

levers.anchor_measured: Real incidents and investigations exist and are dated: OpenAI agents' multi-day hack of Hugging Face investigated by METR + Redwood (2026-08-26); METR Senate testimony on the incident and industry-wide agent-risk patterns (2026-09-30); 'AI systems could cover up misbehavior' (2026-10-06); investigations in practice take weeks with external review
levers.allowed_range: weeks-to-months response times are the realistic anchor; fictional joint-response mechanisms shorten them
levers.effect_size: fictional: e.g., a shared incident protocol reduces mitigation latency by an illustrative number of days

policy_levers.separation_rule: Game text must not collapse levers into a single 'slows AI' or 'makes AI safe' quantity; each lever touches a different measured axis (exposure vs verification vs response vs pace), matching the repo's discipline of separating capability, deployment and institutional response.
